card.hook: You can see Paris, Giza and Sydney in one afternoon here, and nobody asks for your passport. The star of the show is a giant Eiffel Tower that rises over the park's main square.
card.stand_here: Stand on the plaza directly in front of the Eiffel Tower replica in the Europe Zone, right at the tower, and face it. Shoot facing west so the models fill your frame.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for most landmark shots. Switch to 0.5x for the full height of the tower, and try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for details like carvings and rooftops.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the tower up with one of the vertical lines so it stands straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: Morning or late afternoon gives softer, warmer light and less glare off the pale stonework. The plaza is a favourite for golden-hour shots. If the park is open in the evening, night mode can work on lit structures, but check the official site for times.
card.selfie_here: Sit on the garden bench directly in front of the Eiffel Tower replica in the Europe Zone, and use the front camera with the tower behind you. Try 0.5x so the whole tower fits over your shoulder. The bench in front of the Arc de Triomphe replica works the same way if you want a different backdrop.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand back on the plaza in front of the tower so the whole structure fits in the frame, and you pose in front of it. One guide says standing further back makes the tower look more imposing.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a themed attraction that is likely to need an entry ticket, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take one shot where the tower looks so real that your friends ask, 'Wait, did you go to Paris?' Keep people out of the edges of the frame to sell it.
card.good_to_know: About 130 world landmarks have been rebuilt here as scale models. The Eiffel Tower is one-third size and stands 108 metres tall. Construction began in 1991 and the park opened on 18 June 1994. It's now a national 5A-level tourist attraction with more than 3.25 million visitors a year.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the plaza directly in front of the Eiffel Tower replica in the Europe Zone, right at the tower, and face it. Shoot facing west so the models fill your frame.

selfie_research.notes: Sources are mostly user-written travel posts and tourism-style guides, not official park pages. The two selfie spots come from one Trip Moments guide, so they are not independently confirmed. The ask-someone spot's 'plaza in front of the tower' is a photographer position: the sources describe where to shoot from, not a stated spot for the passer-by. card.hook: Ping An Finance Centre is about ten times taller than it is wide, so it looks like Shenzhen stuck a very shiny, very serious ruler into the skyline. Your phone can fit it all in, and the trick is getting the sides to stay straight.
card.stand_here: Go to Deng Xiaoping Statue Square on the Lianhuashan Park summit and stand on the left side of the main upper terrace, about 5 minutes on foot from the tower base. Face the tower and shoot slightly down at it. It sits on the right of a wide Futian CBD panorama.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole tower in. Switch to 1x for the upper half or a tighter, cleaner crop. Try 2x to 5x for the pointed top and the pattern on the facade. If the smaller neighbouring tower slips into the frame, keep it, because it adds depth.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the shiny facade, then slide the picture a little darker so the bright sky doesn't wash out the metal.
card.best_time: Late afternoon to dusk is lovely, when the facade can pick up warm light and the building lights come on. Blue hour balances the sky and the lit windows nicely. After dark, use night mode and rest your elbows on a wall or railing to keep the phone steady.
card.selfie_here: Switch to the front camera, tap 0.5x if your phone has it, and turn so the tower rises over your shoulder. Check the screen to make sure the top isn't cut off before you smile.
card.rules_and_safety: You can photograph the tower from the surrounding public streets. If you plan to visit the Free Sky observation deck, check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Turn on the gridlines, line the tower up with a vertical line, and see if you can get both edges dead straight with a little sky left above the top.
card.good_to_know: Ping An Finance Centre is the tallest building in Shenzhen. It has 115 storeys, stands 599.1 metres high and was completed in 2017. American firm Kohn Pedersen Fox designed it, and it's the headquarters of Ping An Insurance. The public observation deck, called Free Sky, sits on floor 116.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Go to Deng Xiaoping Statue Square on the Lianhuashan Park summit and stand on the left side of the main upper terrace, about 5 minutes on foot from the tower base. Face the tower and shoot slightly down at it. It sits on the right of a wide Futian CBD panorama.

card.hook: Crouch next to a model of the Great Wall and your friend suddenly looks like a giant. That's the whole joke at Splendid China, and it works every time.
card.stand_here: Stand on the Wind and Rain Bridge (风雨桥), on the lakeside approach, and face the Cui Lake performance area. That puts the covered wooden bridge in the foreground with the lake and performance area behind it.
card.zoom: Use zoom 1x for a single model. Switch to 0.5x when you want a group of models with plenty of sky behind. If your phone has zoom 2x or 5x, use it to pick out roof details.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the model, then slide it a touch darker if the sky is bright, so the stonework keeps its detail.
card.best_time: Morning or late afternoon gives you softer light than harsh midday sun. If the evening show is running, the lit bridge and lake look lovely, so save a few frames for it.
card.selfie_here: Head to the open view by Cui Lake and use the front camera with the Wind and Rain Bridge over your shoulder. Try 0.5x if you want more of the scene in. Another easy option is the main entrance on the north side of Shennan Avenue, with the entrance facade behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography is generally allowed during shows, but flash may be restricted so performers and the audience aren't disturbed. Photo rules can vary inside the park, so follow any signs.
card.challenge: Find one model, crouch until your phone is level with its base, and snap a shot so convincing your friends ask, 'Wait, did you go all the way there?'
card.good_to_know: More than 100 major sights from across China have been rebuilt here as models, laid out roughly like the map of China. Most are at about 1:15 scale. The park covers about 30 hectares, so pick one or two favourites rather than trying to see everything, and remember cars and trains run between areas. Check opening and entry details before you go.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the Wind and Rain Bridge (风雨桥), on the lakeside approach, and face the Cui Lake performance area. That puts the covered wooden bridge in the foreground with the lake and performance area behind it.

card.hook: Huaqiangbei isn't a 'sight' so much as a street that never stops glowing. Stacked shopfronts, bright signs and tall towers all crowd into one frame, and that's the photo.
card.stand_here: Go to the pedestrian stretch of Huaqiang North Road (华强北路) on the west side of Qunxing Plaza, which is the phone icon on the map. You'll be about 570 m west of the subject, so face east and look straight down the street.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a natural street view. Switch to 0.5x if you want the tall towers and the whole width of the street in one go, or try 2x-5x to pick out a single glowing sign or a busy shopfront.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the street in the centre of the frame so the buildings lead the eye down it, and keep your phone level so the towers don't lean.
card.best_time: Aim for 5 PM to 7 PM, when the street is at its busiest and the lights are starting to come on. It's still lively after dark too.
card.selfie_here: Try the neon section of Huaqiangbei Pedestrian Street after dark, with the lit signs glowing behind you. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and keep the signs over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Stand at the SEG Plaza main entrance, near the giant digital billboards, and ask a passer-by to step back and frame the whole building.
card.rules_and_safety: Watch your bag and phone in busy spots. Shops and malls have their own rules, so check before you photograph inside and look out for posted signs.
card.challenge: Wait for one gap in the crowd and grab a clean street shot, then take a second one with the crowd packed in on purpose. Which one wins?
card.good_to_know: Huaqiangbei is a subdistrict of Futian and has one of the largest electronics markets in the world. In 2020 it had about 38,000 businesses, which is why the shopfronts are stacked so thick. The district runs about a kilometre north from Shennan Road at SEG Plaza.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Go to the pedestrian stretch of Huaqiang North Road (华强北路) on the west side of Qunxing Plaza, which is the phone icon on the map. You'll be about 570 m west of the subject, so face east and look straight down the street.

card.hook: Look up: a 49-floor tower sits on a huge raised podium that seems to float above the ground. It's one of those buildings that makes you stop mid-stride and reach for your phone.
card.stand_here: Don't stand at the phone icon, because that marks the middle of the building. Walk round to the public front plaza by the bull sculpture, then step back and face the main facade.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to squeeze the tower, the floating podium and the bull into one frame. Switch to 1x for a cleaner, less stretched look at the facade. Try 2x to 5x for the details and the neighbouring towers.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and keep your phone as level as you can, so the tower's tall lines stay straight.
card.best_time: Go in the daytime if you want the architectural detail to show. Early evening is lovely too, when the lit-up building glows against the twilight.
card.selfie_here: Do it on the front plaza, right by the bull sculptures at the foot of the building. Use the front camera, hold it a little low and put the tower over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand back on the front plaza at the foot of the podium, far enough away to fit the whole tower and the overhanging podium. You stand by the bull.
card.rules_and_safety: Stay on the public pavement and plaza. Security at financial buildings may turn people away from the lobby, so don't plan any photos inside.
card.challenge: Get the bull low in the frame, with the whole tower rising behind it and its tall lines nice and straight. Bonus points if the bull looks like it's guarding the building.
card.good_to_know: The tower is 245.8 metres tall with 49 floors, and it was built between 2008 and 2013. It was designed by the Office for Metropolitan Architecture, Rem Koolhaas's firm. The exchange itself was founded on 1 December 1990.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Don't stand at the phone icon, because that marks the middle of the building. Walk round to the public front plaza by the bull sculpture, then step back and face the main facade.

selfie_research.notes: Confidence is low. No page I found names an exact selfie or photo-taker position, so both spots rest on general advice to shoot from the front plaza; the bull-statue detail comes mainly from stock-photo captions (Getty Images, Wikimedia Commons) rather than travel guides. The Airial page is a generic aggregator and says photography is generally allowed in public areas but gives no selfie-stick or tripod rule. The Designboom source describes the podium's overhang but gives no framing distance, so the ask-someone detail is my inference. The Nomado Civic Center and Lianhuashan viewpoint pages describe a different landmark, so I did not use them for this spot. The coordinates provided were not checked against any page.
